title: fix(app-shell): the permission editor's row-level-security policy list draws each policy's label and description (objectui#11199)
body:
Fixes #11199
Clause-②: no

## What changed

`PermissionAdvancedFacets` is the permission edit page's own row-level-security policy list. Each policy card now starts with that policy's `label` and, below it, its `description`, shown as written. A policy that declares neither, or declares them as empty strings, renders the same card as before. Nothing new is authored: the two keys are shown, not edited.

- **Types.** The facet's `RlsPolicy` now takes `label` and `description` from `RowLevelSecurityPolicy` in `@objectstack/spec/security` (via `Pick`) instead of restating them. The spec declares both as plain optional strings, not I18nLabel, so they render as written with no locale lookup. No new catalogue strings were needed: the claim expected en / zh strings, but the caption holds only author text.
- **Surface.** The fix is in the facet. `PermissionPreview` is not mounted on the edit page, per the triage direction: the facet is the surface an author edits on, and it needs only eight lines of markup to show both values.

## Step 1: booted Studio gate (before the change)

- **Backend:** the objectstack `main` `1741c5dcb` showcase, run as `objectstack dev --seed-admin --fresh -p 4719` from a detached scratch worktree.
- **Console:** this branch's worktree at objectui `846cec0ef`, run as `vite --port 5719 --strictPort` with `DEV_PROXY_TARGET` pointing at the backend.
- **Fixture:** the showcase set `showcase_contributor`. Each of its three RLS policies declares a label and a description, and the stored `row_level_security` column, read back over REST, carries both.

A Playwright probe logged in as the seeded admin and expanded the RLS section. It then searched `document.body.innerText`, `page.content()` and every input's live value for the two labels (`Own Tasks Only`, `Own Invoices Only`) and the two descriptions.

| Surface | label / description shown, before | control: policy name `task_own_rows` found |
|---|---|---|
| Studio Access pillar, `/studio/com.example.showcase/access` | no / no | yes (input value) |
| `/apps/studio/metadata/permission/showcase_contributor` | no / no | yes |
| `/apps/setup/metadata/permission/showcase_contributor` | no / no | yes |
| Setup record page of the `sys_permission_set` row | no / no | not applicable: the page shows "3 RLS policies" and a Design-in-Studio link |

The premise held: neither value was shown anywhere. The control column proves the probe reached the expanded policy list.

After the change, the same probe on the same boot finds both labels and both descriptions on all three edit surfaces. The Setup record page is unchanged, because it summarises the facet as a count by design.

## Mechanism assumptions, measured

1. **No loss on save.** `stripRetiredRlsKeys` deletes only the retired `priority`. Every write path spreads the whole policy (`{ ...pol, name }`), so `label` and `description` survive an edit. The third test below pins this round trip.
2. **Reading shape.** The keys are typed from the spec symbol, not from a third local shape. The render guard is a truthiness check on a spec `string | undefined`. It gives the same result as `PermissionPreview`'s `authoredText`: an absent or empty value renders nothing.
3. **Plain strings.** Both keys are `z.string().optional()` on `RowLevelSecurityPolicySchema`, both in the installed spec 17.5.0 and on objectstack `main`. They are not I18nLabel, so they render as written.
4. **Editing is not built.** The card asks only that the values be shown. An edit input beside the caption would be a small addition; the report names it as an option.

## Tests

The new pin `PermissionAdvancedFacets.rlsLabelDescription.test.tsx` has three tests:
- A labelled policy's label and description render inside its own card, and not inside a neighbouring bare policy's card.
- Control: a bare policy, and a policy with empty-string label and description, each keep the two card children they had before (the input row and the USING / CHECK grid). The labelled card has three.
- Editing the policy name keeps `label` and `description` on the emitted draft.

**Ablation**, at `af886d1bf`, through `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs` in WRAP mode:
- The description draw was replaced with `null`. Result: `Tests 1 failed | 2 passed (3)`. The failing test reported "Unable to find an element with the text: Contributors can only select tasks assigned to them."
- The restore was proven: blob equals HEAD and `git diff HEAD` is empty.
- The prediction was red on exactly that one test, which is what happened.

**Local runs**, all at `af886d1bf`:
- **Targeted vitest**, run from the repo root with path filters: the `PermissionAdvancedFacets*`, `PermissionMatrixEditor*`, `previews/PermissionPreview*`, `permission-slice*`, `CelPredicateField*` and `CelTestRunDialog*` suites, plus `src/__tests__/spec-symbol-parity.test.ts`, plugin-designer's `MetadataFieldsPage.saveEnvelope.test.tsx` and `scripts/__tests__/spec-symbol-ledger-app-shell-7265.test.ts`. Result: `Test Files 34 passed (34)`, `Tests 263 passed (263)`.
- **Closure build**, `pnpm exec turbo run build --filter='@object-ui/app-shell^...' --concurrency=2`: exit 0.
- **Type-check**, `pnpm --filter @object-ui/app-shell type-check` (runs `tsc --noEmit && tsc -p tsconfig.test.json`): exit 0. `--listFilesOnly` confirms both changed files are in those programs.
- **Root scripts suite**, `pnpm exec vitest run scripts/__tests__/`: `Test Files 177 passed | 2 skipped (179)`, `Tests 5371 passed | 2 skipped (5373)`. It ran because the changeset is a markdown file; `node scripts/markdown-test-inputs.mjs --audit` also exited 0.
- **eslint** on the two changed files: 0 errors and 3 warnings. All three warnings are on lines outside this diff's hunks: the existing `setDraft` prop type's `any`, and an existing effect.
- **Gates**, all exit 0: `node scripts/check-changeset-presence.mjs`, `pnpm check:control-bytes`, `pnpm check:new-line-citations` (0 new citations), `pnpm check:spec-symbols` and `pnpm check:i18n-keys`.
- **Declared narrowings:**
  - The vitest run covered the suites that render or read the facet, not the whole `metadata-admin/` directory; the full farm is CI's.
  - The targeted vitest run and the single-file ablation ran without the shared verify lock, because a sibling's hold passed 30 minutes. The closure build, type-check and scripts suite ran under the lock.

**Re-run at the merged head `c9c960eed`:** targeted vitest `Test Files 34 passed (34)`, `Tests 263 passed (263)`; `check-changeset-presence`, `check:control-bytes`, `check:new-line-citations`, `check:spec-symbols`, `check:i18n-keys` and `markdown-test-inputs --audit` exit 0.

## Acceptance notes

- **For objectstack-ai/objectstack#20299** (the two liveness rows): the mounted reader is the `PermissionAdvancedFacets` symbol in `packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/PermissionAdvancedFacets.tsx`, where each policy card's caption reads `pol.label` and `pol.description`. It has one direct mount, reached from two routes:
  - `PermissionMatrixEditPage` in `PermissionMatrixEditor.tsx`, registered as the `permission` `EditPage` in `services/builtinComponents.tsx`;
  - the Studio Access pillar (`AccessPillar` in `StudioDesignSurface.tsx`), which mounts `PermissionMatrixEditPage` embedded. A citation names the direct mount above.
- `PermissionPreview` is still not mounted by any production route for `permission`. This PR does not change that.
- The test-run dialog (`CelTestRunDialog`) still names a policy by its `name`. That is outside this card.
- The Row-Level Security section of `packages/app-shell/README.md` documents CEL authoring safety and does not list what a card contains, so it is unchanged.
- **CI:** this head carries `main`'s objectui#11206 fix (`9419df198`, merged in as `c9c960eed`), and `Spec Main Shape Gate` is green on it.
